To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the shareholder primacy conception of corporate purpose has been dominant for a long time; (2) the hostile takeover movement in the 1980s led to a temporary shift in corporate governance toward a more shareholder-friendly model; and (3) the shift was not a permanent one and was reversed by the late 1990s, with the shareholder primacy view reasserting itself as the dominant view.

(a) shareholder primacy is not the only conception of corporate purpose; (b) shareholder primacy has been discredited by the hostile takeover experience; and (c) the hostile takeover experience was not a failure because it produced a more efficient allocation of capital.

(1) the market for corporate control is an inefficient means of corporate governance; and (2) the market for control is a means by which corporate managers are able to resist shareholder pressure for higher returns.

the question of whether the shareholder primacy norm should be replaced by an alternative norm that gives more weight to the interests of other corporate constituents, such as employees, customers, and communities.
